question: Which statement best describes The document frame?
options: The `<html>` element wraps the whole document and can identify its language with a `lang` attribute. For example, use `lang="en"` for an English page. The language helps assistive technology choose pronunciation rules and helps other tools interpret the content. The root language should reflect the page’s primary language. If a passage changes language, mark that section when pronunciation needs to change. The html element is like a book cover that holds every page.

The `<body>` contains visible page content, such as headings, paragraphs, forms, and controls. Keep the main content here and use elements whose meaning matches their role. This separation helps browsers and assistive tools distinguish document setup from the page people read and use. Use semantic elements inside the body for headings, navigation, forms, and main content. The body is not a reason to put every item in a generic div. The body is like the readable pages inside the cover.

The `<head>` holds metadata, such as the title, character encoding, viewport, and links to stylesheets. Most head contents are not shown as the article itself. Declare UTF-8 so punctuation and international text decode correctly, and include a viewport setting for mobile layouts. Metadata belongs in the head, while readable content belongs in the body. This separation makes page structure and browser settings easier to locate. The head is like a catalog card that describes the book before it is opened.

`<!doctype html>` tells the browser to use modern HTML rules. It is a declaration at the start of the file, not visible page content. It helps the browser avoid legacy rendering modes. Place it before the `<html>` element so the document begins predictably. The doctype helps select standards mode. It is a short declaration at the top, not a tag that wraps page content.
explanation: `<!doctype html>` tells the browser to use modern HTML rules. It is a declaration at the start of the file, not visible page content. It helps the browser avoid legacy rendering modes. Place it before the `<html>` element so the document begins predictably. The doctype helps select standards mode. It is a short declaration at the top, not a tag that wraps page content.
